messages.subject: Structural TVAR estimation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Matthieu,
I'm Valeria Patella and I've just graduated in Economics. I'm working with non linear multivariate models and I found very helpful the tsDyn package for TVAR estimation and LR testing for linearity. However, in order to assign an economic interpretation to stochastic simulations (working with structural shocks), I need to estimate the structural form of the model, applying some restrictions on the contemporaneous correlations of the system. In particular, I work with the AB identification strategy. Should I need to modify manually the code of TVAR function or is there some already made function? Can you give me some advice?
I would really appreciate your help
Cordially,
Valeria Patella

messages.subject: Re: Structural TVAR estimation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Valeria

Unofortunately, tsDyn does not provide functions for structural VAR/VECM. So you will have to do this on your own, either by modifiying the TVAR code from tsDyn to do T-SVAR or maybe instead starting from the code of package vars, using the code of SVAR to make it a T-SVAR... not sure which approach will be faster for you, depends how familiar you are with threshold vs. SVAR models.

Good luck

Matthieu

PS: not sure your membership request to tsDyn worked, if not, don't hesitate to do it a second time!

2013/7/12 Valeria Patella <valeria....@gmail.com>

messages.subject: New version(s) 0.9, 0.9-1... 0.9-3
messages.body_plain:
Dear List

I just submitted a new version of tsDyn, 0.9-32, which will be available on CRAN in a few hours/days. I realised that I haven't notified the updated version since version 0.8, so there is quite a big list of new features/bug fixes/changes. The whole list is described in the Changelog, which is available now on github:
https://github.com/MatthieuStigler/tsDyn/blob/master/tsDyn/inst/ChangeLog

To summarise, the major changes are around linear VAR/VECM functions, as well as forecasting functions. These are:

-linear functions:
   -tsDyn has now its proper rank.test() function, as well as rank.select() function, to select lags and rank simultaneously by AIC/BIC.
   -fevd() and irf() from package vars are now wrapped
   -VARrep() showing VAR representaiton of a VECM

-forecasting functions:
   - a predict function is available now for VAR/VECM
   - a new rolling_predict allowing to do rolling forecasts, varying the time period and horizon.
   - a accuracy_stat() function to give standard forecasting accuracy measures, works also together with rolling_predict()

I also used the github facility to write a very minimalist wiki, as well as a FAQ: https://github.com/MatthieuStigler/tsDyn/wiki/FAQ
The FAQ is very minimal for now, but if anyone want to add something, please feel free!!!

Best

Matthieu
